title: Mara River Crossings: When and Where to See Them
excerpt: The Mara River crossings are the most dramatic moments of the Great Migration. When and where they happen, and how to improve your chances.
body:
A river crossing is what many people picture when they think of the migration: thousands of wildebeest plunging into the Mara River, with crocodiles waiting.

## When

Mara River crossings usually take place from around July to October. The exact timing changes every year.

## Where

In the northern Serengeti, around Kogatende and Lamai, and in the Masai Mara in Kenya. Smaller crossings happen at the Grumeti River in June. See [the northern Serengeti](/blog/northern-serengeti-kogatende/).

## What happens

Herds gather on the riverbank, sometimes for hours. Then one animal jumps, and the rest follow. A crossing can last minutes or more than an hour.

## Patience

Crossings are unpredictable. You can wait a whole morning without one, and then see two in the afternoon. Spending at least three nights in the north increases your chances.

## Ethics

Rules say vehicles must keep distance and not block the herds. Choose a guide who respects that.

## Photography

See [photographing the Great Migration](/blog/migration-photography-tips/).
